classification.difficultyReason: Translate overlapping enrolment totals into exclusive Venn regions, calculate neither from the total, and read the requested regions as probabilities.

inlines.text: Use an appropriate Venn diagram in the following questions.
In a group of 100 students, 60 study mathematics, 70 study physics and 30 study both mathematics and physics.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: $M$: mathematics; $P$: physics. Mathematics only: 30; both: 30; physics only: 40; neither: 0.
answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the event ‘studies mathematics’ and $P$ be the event ‘studies physics’. Bracketed numbers in the diagram give the number of students in each region.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Mathematics only}&=60-30\\\text{Mathematics only}&=30\\\text{Physics only}&=70-30\\\text{Physics only}&=40\\\text{Neither}&=100-(30+30+40)\\\text{Neither}&=0\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9(a); teacher PDF page 38, Exercise 12B Question 9(a)
spec.description: Two overlapping circles labelled M and P inside the sample-space rectangle. Counts are bracketed as taught in Example 5. The zero outside both circles is made explicit.
spec.mathematics: M only = 30; M intersection P = 30; P only = 40; neither = 0; total = 100.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student must construct the diagram.

children.label: b
children.prompt: One student is selected at random from the group. What is the probability that the student studies:

answer.worked:
From the Venn diagram, 30 students study mathematics and not physics.

$$\begin{align*}P(M\cap P^c)&=\frac{30}{100}\\P(M\cap P^c)&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$

From the Venn diagram, 40 students study physics but not mathematics.

$$\begin{align*}P(P\cap M^c)&=\frac{40}{100}\\P(P\cap M^c)&=\frac{2}{5}\end{align*}$$

There are no students outside both circles.

$$P(P^c\cap M^c)=\frac{0}{100}=0.$$
